units.title: Construct consecutive non-perfect-powers by CRT
units.statement: For distinct primes p_i, CRT gives N+i congruent to p_i modulo p_i squared, making every N+i divisible by p_i exactly once and therefore not a perfect power. For any d at least 2, d divides the central binomial coefficient with a=d-1 because it is coprime to 2d-1.
steps: Choose distinct primes and impose one congruence modulo each prime square
Apply CRT to obtain a block of consecutive integers
Use the binomial identity with 2d-1 to choose a=d-1
